uncertainObservations: The number of swords in the figure's arms is my least certain reading. The hilts overlap and sit against a dark cloak; I can distinguish what look like three pommel/crossguard groups, but two or four is possible. Recorded as 3 with low confidence rather than guessed higher.

I cannot confirm that the carried objects are swords rather than staffs or spears; I can see crossguard-like forms at the top and tapering blades below, which is why I call them swords, but the blades fade into shadow.
The two planted uprights at left and right are clearly blade-shaped with crossguards, but I cannot see their points entering the ground on the left one.
The two structures read as stone pyramids, but they could equally be steep tents or roofed shelters; the surface texture is ambiguous.
The figure's head is turned back and down but I cannot read any facial features or confirm the direction of the eyes.
Whether there is anything inside the two dark doorways is not resolvable.
The pale glow on the back wall has no visible source; I cannot tell if it is moonlight, a fire out of frame, or a window.

issues.existing: the figure's body moves away while its head turns back
issues.observed: I cannot find any evidence of a backward glance on this card. The head is drawn as a featureless rear silhouette: the back of the skull faces the viewer, rim-lit along its upper-left edge, with no face, eye, ear or profile visible on either side at any magnification. A head turned back would present a profile toward the viewer-left; none is drawn. In my blind pass I recorded the head as aligned with the body, i.e. facing the direction of travel, and noted that the gaze direction is simply not determinable. The same claim is restated in emphasizedAspects as 'a backward glance that keeps watch on what is left behind'.
issues.evidence: Head, roughly x=230-330 / y=320-400 in the 560x933 image. Enlarged 9x and brightened 3.4x it resolves only to a mass of shaggy dark hair with highlights along the top-left; the lower-right of the mass, where a cheek or jaw would fall if the head were turned back, holds no recoverable detail. For contrast, review-512 draws its backward glance explicitly, with a full three-quarter face turned opposite to the direction of travel — nothing comparable exists here.

uncertainObservations: This is the darkest of the eight. I brightened it more than three times over and large parts of the frame still hold no recoverable detail; several readings here are low-confidence.
The number of carried swords cannot be determined: three grips plus one cross-guard are resolvable, a fourth may be hidden, and the blade count below the hand reads as three or four.
No face is visible at all, so I cannot say whether he is looking ahead, down or back — I can only say the head is not turned back toward the viewer.
Whether the two structures are stone cairns/tombs, shingled huts or stiffened tents is ambiguous; they have doorways and roof finials.
The source of the upper-left glow is not drawn; it could be a moon behind cloud, a lamp out of frame or a lit opening.
I cannot confirm whether the planted swords' points are driven into the earth or merely hidden behind foreground stones.
